decisions.reason: The Trivital range is an umbrella brand sold through the pharmacy channel the firm already knows well, so it can interpret market feedback and keep the range, even though supplements sit outside its core pharmaceutical R&D.

The skin and hair supplement relies on the firm's pharmacy marketing know-how and was presented on its own page, but its weak link to the firm's drug R&D and a crowded beauty-supplement market make it a moderate drop risk.

Joint health is a steady pharmacy category where the firm's pharmaceutical knowledge helps it formulate and position the product, and it moved from a mention to its own page in 2019, so keeping it is reasonable.
The mushroom-based immune concept is furthest from the firm's existing knowledge, but immune products gained demand during the pandemic, which gives a reason to keep it for now.

The 2018 valsartan contamination recall harmed this generic, but generics registration and quality control are core competences the firm can use to fix the supply problem, so it stays despite an elevated risk.
An over-the-counter migraine triptan builds directly on the firm's pharmaceutical and neurological OTC expertise, so it fits the firm's absorptive capacity and should be kept.
